resources.string: Disconnect
Disconnect %1$s?
The data and backups stay intact, but no new backups will be saved. To use earlier ones, go to Find a file.
The password is deleted from this phone, but it stays valid on the service. It is cancelled there.
Cloud disconnected
Could not disconnect. Everything is as it was.
Sign in to %1$s
The %1$s session ended, and backups are stopped. Once signed in they continue on their own, with no new files. Until then, anything new is only on this phone.
%1$s could not be opened from here. Open that app by hand and sign in.
There are already %1$d pinned backups. Release one to continue.
The backup from %1$s comes from another phone. Backups were stopped so nothing is lost.
The backup from %1$s is newer than what is on this phone. Backups were stopped so nothing is lost.
This phone has fewer records than the last backup, and information may be missing. Backups were stopped so nothing is lost.
All three backups in %1$s are protected, and a new backup would have to replace one of them. Backups were stopped so nothing is lost.
%1$s was changed outside %2$s. Backups were stopped so nothing is lost.
In the cloud: %1$s, %2$s, %3$s. On this phone: %4$s and %5$s.
%1$s does not know what %2$s contains, so that side has no date or records. On this phone: %3$s and %4$s.
Restore the cloud backup
It replaces what is here. What is current stays in a local copy.
That file is opened with Find a file. It replaces what is here, and what is current stays in a local copy.
Keep this phone
The next backup will be the most recent. The cloud backup stays pinned.
The next backup will be the most recent. %1$s keeps that cloud backup while it has more records, or more products, customers and suppliers, than the new one.
%1$s does not write over %2$s. A new file must be created in %3$s, and %2$s stays there untouched.
Decide later
Work can continue, but no backups are saved.
Keep this phone?
On this phone: %1$s. In the backup from %2$s: %3$s. That backup stops being the most recent, but it stays pinned and %4$s does not delete it.

On this phone: %1$s. In the backup from %2$s: %3$s. That backup stops being the most recent. It is not pinned: %4$s keeps it while it has more records, or more products, customers and suppliers, than the new one.
On this phone: %1$s. To continue, a new file is created in %2$s. %3$s stays there untouched, and it opens with Find a file. Without the new file, nothing changes.
